title: Slow-cooker birria tacos
cook: 8 hr on low, plus 30 min for the tacos

items: 3 lb boneless beef chuck roast, trimmed of thick fat and cut into 4 large chunks
1½ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
4 dried guajillo chiles and 2 dried ancho chiles, stems and seeds removed (or 3 Tbsp chili powder)
1 medium white onion, half roughly chopped and half finely diced
1 tsp dried oregano (Mexican if you have it)
12 oz Oaxaca or low-moisture mozzarella cheese, shredded (about 3 cups)
Finely diced onion (the reserved half from above)

steps: Put the stemmed, seeded chiles in the heatproof bowl, cover with the 2 cups boiling water and soak 10–15 min, until soft and bendable. Drain and discard the water. If you're using chili powder, skip this step.
Blend the soaked chiles (or chili powder), chipotle, the roughly chopped onion, garlic, cumin, oregano, 1½ tsp salt and the broth on high 1–2 min, until completely smooth.
Season the beef with a little salt and put it in the slow cooker. Pour the sauce over it. Cover and cook on low 8 hr, until the beef falls apart when pressed with a fork (about 200°F inside).

Lift the beef onto a cutting board and shred it with 2 forks, discarding any fat. Skim the red fat from the top of the broth into a small bowl. Taste the broth and add salt if needed. Toss the meat with ½ cup broth.
Heat the skillet over medium heat. Dip a tortilla in the red fat, or quickly in the broth, and lay it in the pan. Cover half with about 2 Tbsp cheese and 2–3 Tbsp beef.
Cook 2–3 min, until the tortilla is crisp underneath and the cheese melts. Fold it closed and cook about 1 min per side, until crisp on both sides. Repeat, cooking 2–3 at a time if they fit.
Ladle the hot broth into small cups. Serve the tacos with the broth for dipping, plus diced onion, cilantro and lime wedges.
tips: Use a fully thawed roast. Frozen meat stays too cold for too long in a slow cooker.
For deeper flavor, sear the beef chunks in 1 Tbsp oil in a hot skillet 3–4 min per side before they go in.
No slow cooker: braise covered in a Dutch oven at 325°F for 3–3½ hr, until it falls apart.
storage: Store the meat and broth separately. Fridge up to 4 days or freezer up to 3 months. Reheat the broth in a pot until simmering and the meat in a covered skillet with a splash of broth. Make the tacos fresh.
